def: A fixed set of documents, queries and relevance judgements used to compare retrieval systems repeatably (the Cranfield paradigm).
Query relevance labels: the file of judged (query, document, grade) triples that metrics are computed against.
What the user actually wants to know or do, written down beside the query string so judges resolve ambiguity the same way.
Judging only the union of the top results from several different retrieval systems, and treating everything else as non-relevant.
How many top results from each contributing system are added to the pool for judging.
The share of a system's top-k results that have no relevance judgement, a measure of how fairly the pool covers that system.
Agreement between two judges corrected for the agreement expected by chance, from 0 (chance) to 1 (perfect).
A kappa for graded labels in which disagreements between nearby grades count as less serious than distant ones.
Settling judges' disagreements by a third person or discussion, recording the reason and keeping the original labels.
The thing the system returns and judges label: a file, page, section or chunk.
A short document recording how a dataset was built, sampled, labelled and checked, and what it should and should not be used for.
